lesson_title: The Axis That Lies: How Honest Numbers Fool Your Eyes
hook_text: Every number on this graph is true — and it's still lying to you. Catch the trick in 5 seconds.
clip_script: A chart compares January's 320 units with June's 575 — but its number axis begins at 300 instead of nought. What survives of January above the 300 line? A stub of 20. Of June? A column of 275. The column stands nearly fourteen times the stub, and your eye shouts that winter usage exploded. The actual numbers say June is not even double January. The lie lives in the missing bottom of the picture — the region where both months stood level was chopped away, so only the difference got drawn. It is a photograph cropped down to the scowl. Your defence takes five seconds: check where the axis starts. If it is not nought, read the true values and redo the comparison yourself.
visual_style: A bar chart sliced off at 300 by animated scissors, bars morphing from a shocking 14-to-1 illusion to the honest side-by-side truth as the axis slides back down to zero.
pacing: Shock reveal first, slow-motion mechanism, snappy five-second defence at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to turn any graph into money decisions you can defend.
